thread.title: Spotify continues to pick up fans on Wall Street in stock's first week of trading

author: morningstar.com
title: Spotify continues to pick up fans on Wall Street in stock's first week of trading
text:
By Emily Bary
At least six analysts have initiated coverage of Spotify with buy ratings
Even before shares of Spotify Technology SA began trading, several Wall Street analysts chimed in with their recommendations on the stock.
It's unusual for analysts, particularly at big firms, to publish recommendations on stocks before trading begins, or even in the first couple of weeks of trading, due to quiet periods imposed on underwriting firms. But because Spotify chose to forego a traditional initial public offering in favor of a direct listing, the company didn't raise any money from Wall Street, so many analysts have been free to comment away.
At least six analysts have initiated coverage of Spotify with buy ratings, according to FactSet, while three others rate the stock a hold.
Don't miss: 5 things to know about Spotify's direct listing (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/spotify-ipo-5-things-to-know-about-the-streaming-music-giants-direct-listing-2018-03-02)
RBC Capital Markets analyst Mark Mahaney is the biggest Spotify bull so far, with an overweight rating and a $220 price target, or about 46% above its current trading level. He likes Spotify's standing (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/spotify-initiated-at-outperform-by-rbc-ahead-of-trading-debut-2018-03-29) as the leading subscription streaming service and thinks the company can withstand competition from tech giants like Apple Inc. (AAPL) and Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN).
"We see several factors that should help Spotify maintain its leadership," he wrote, including a strong brand and a "platform-neutral presence."
Spotify has the top music app on Android and Apple phones in at least half of the top 20 markets, not including China, he said. Mahaney also points to Spotify's well-received personalization efforts and the variety brought about by its paid and free tiers.
See also: Three ways Apple could spend $163 billion besides a big acquisition (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/three-ways-apple-could-spend-163-billion-besides-a-big-acquisition-2018-03-16)
Mahaney sees room for Spotify to expand its gross margin as it continues to secure better terms with the labels and benefits from the further scaling of its ad business. Spotify's gross margin rose to 21% last year from 14% a year earlier, and the company is targeting margins of 30% to 35% for the long term.
MKM Partners analyst Rob Sanderson also predicts "a much larger margin opportunity" for Spotify, though he thinks that margin expansion won't necessarily come "at the expense of music label profits." Sanderson is intrigued by the fact that more than 30% of streams are programmed, rather than directly requested.
"We expect Spotify will increasingly work with labels to promote artists and that labels will excuse royalty obligations from promotional content," Sanderson wrote. "This can be considered marketing expense by labels, which typically allocate 15% to 20% of revenue to marketing functions."
"We are anticipating unusual trading dynamics in the days and weeks following the April 3 listing and are unsure how long before adequate liquidity will be established," wrote Sanderson, who has a $200 price target (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/spotify-gets-another-bullish-analyst-call-ahead-of-ipo-2018-03-29) and a buy rating on the stock. "Our target is a 12-month view independent of potential supply/demand irregularities on low trading volume immediately following the listing."
Related: IPO proceeds hit 3-year high in first quarter, fueled by foreign offerings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ipo-proceeds-hit-a-3-year-high-in-the-first-quarter-boosted-by-foreign-companies-2018-03-29)
James Cordwell of Atlantic Equities is also upbeat on the stock, beginning coverage with an overweight rating and a $160 year-end price target. Cordwell points out that Spotify's average revenue per user, or ARPU, has been falling as more users pack onto family plans, which has shifted the company's business model more toward a "per household" one.
That said, he notes that Spotify has been able to post strong revenue growth even amid the declines in ARPU, which he expects to become less significant "as the pace of the mix shift to family plans moderates."
Cordwell echoed the optimism about margin-expansion potential, writing that he models Spotify turning profitable in 2020 while generating a 28.3% gross margin.
Stifel's John Egbert, who initiated coverage with a buy rating on Thursday, likened the company to a young Netflix Inc. (NFLX). "We think Spotify can deliver meaningful operating profits and cash flow within the constraints of its current licensing structure, with additional upside if the company is successful with its endeavors in demand creation and / or non-music content," he wrote. "Similar to Netflix, when the company was early on in its transition from DVDs to streaming video, Spotify's margin structure appears far from optimized today."
Egbert assigned a $180 price target (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/spotify-initiated-with-buy-rating-at-stifel-2018-04-05) to shares.
Canaccord Genuity's Maria Ripps also opted for a Netflix comparison, writing that "we see several similarities between Spotify and Netflix (global reach and strong subscriber outlook), as well as some differences (proprietary content for Netflix, less so for Spotify)." Ripps sees room for both Pandora Media Inc. (P) and Spotify to emerge as winners in the "growing market" for streaming music. She initiated coverage of Spotify with a buy rating and a $200 price target, while assuming coverage of Pandora with a buy rating and $7 target.
Gabelli & Co.'s John Tinker stayed on the sidelines, starting coverage of Spotify's stock at hold on Tuesday. "Apple is growing faster than Spotify and has a different business model whereby music does not have to be profitable on a standalone basis," Tinker wrote (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/spotify-initiated-with-hold-at-gabelli-analyst-worries-about-apple-competition-record-label-leverage-2018-04-03). He expressed some concern on profits, writing that "scale does not translate into higher margins as two-thirds of revenue continue to be paid as royalties."
Spotify shares were up 3.4% on Thursday, while the S&P 500 was up 0.8%.
-Emily Bary;
